description: Fork of exp729 (FastMHL hard fwd + NAP+1 ball bwd, 1.2360 hard SOTA). Single change: backward_mode 'ball' -> 'dense_K'. Tests whether widening the backward from NAP+1 rows (main + Hamming-1 neighbours) to all K=2^NAP rows (softmax-weighted full surrogate) helps the LUT train better under native hard forward. Hypothesis: with no soft->hard distribution shift (hard fwd is the deployment mode), the only question is which backward keeps more LUT rows usefully trained. K-row dense gives gradient to every row weighted by exp(-distance/T), while ball gives only NAP+1 rows. Bench (out_proj NAP=7, B=12288): hard/dense_K = 22.9 ms vs hard/ball = 21.2 ms (+8%). Estimated wallclock ~5.3 h vs exp729's 4.94 h. Everything else identical: E=384 NAP-bump arch, 16k steps, bs=24 ga=2, Lion lr=2e-4 for LUT, AdamW 3e-4 elsewhere, soft_score_temp=select_temp=0.5, learnable temps, use_bf16=True.
